name: AD8264ACPZ-R7
title: Quad dc-coupled linear-in-dB VGA with preamp and differential output amplifier, 235 MHz
summary: The AD8264 holds four independent channels, each a 6 dB preamp, a 0 dB to 24 dB linear-in-dB variable gain stage and a 6 dB single-ended-to-differential output amplifier, all dc coupled. Gain follows 20 dB/V of the voltage between each channel's GNHx and a shared GNLO, giving 0 dB to 24 dB to the VGA output and 6 dB to 30 dB to the differential output. The output common mode (VOCM) and a per-channel differential offset (OFSx) let it drive a dc-coupled ADC directly, which suits pulse processing in PET, ultrasound, radar and multichannel data acquisition. It runs from ±2.5 V to ±5 V in a 40-lead 6 mm LFCSP.
key_figures: 0 dB to 24 dB to VGAx; 6 dB to 30 dB to differential output

notes: Z marks a RoHS-compliant part.

circuits.title: Gain set by a 10-bit DAC, output into a 12-bit ADC
circuits.description: One AD8264 channel feeding a 1.8 V ADC with the gains set by a 10-bit DAC, all from ±3.3 V. An ADR127 on +3.3 V makes 1.25 V; it is the DAC's reference and, halved by two 1 kΩ 1 % resistors (0.1 µF on the tap), biases GNLO at 625 mV so the DAC's 0 V to 1.25 V output spans the whole ±0.625 V gain control range. DAC outputs D, C, B and A drive GNH1 to GNH4. The ADC's SENSE pin is grounded, so its VREF pin puts out 1 V, which sets VOCM (10 µF and 0.1 µF to ground): both outputs sit at 1 V, OFSx is grounded, and the ADC sees 2 V p-p full scale through an RFILT-CFILT-RFILT anti-alias filter. VOLx goes to VIN-, VOHx to VIN+. VGAx is free for other processing.

parts.value: VGA output to other signal processing

notes: Channel x is drawn as channel 1 (IPP1, GNH1, OFS1, VGA1, VOL1, VOH1).
Each DAC output ranges 0 V to 1.25 V; VOUT = VREFIN × D / 2^N.
About 1 µA leaves the GNLO pin and about 250 nA each GNHx pin.
The ADR127 supplies 625 µA to the divider; the DAC reference input draws about 28 µA (45 kΩ nominal).
For two AD8264s the same divider serves (about 2 µA of bias, 1 mV of error, 0.02 dB). Several AD8264s on one ADC VREF need a buffer on VREF.
U2 pins 1, 5 and 6 are NC.

circuits.title: PET pulse channel with a 40-channel DAC and a 12-bit ADC
circuits.description: A PET front end: the PMT's negative current pulse makes 0 V to -0.1 V across 100 Ω at IPPx. GNLO is grounded and each GNHx comes from a 40-channel DAC (0 V to 2.5 V out with the 1.25 V ADR127 reference) through a scale circuit: two 49.9 kΩ 1 % resistors from the DAC output to -1.25 V, the midpoint (0.1 µF to ground) driving GNHx over -0.625 V to +0.625 V. An AD8663 with two 49.9 kΩ resistors inverts the 1.25 V reference to -1.25 V (10 µF and 0.1 µF). At 20× (26 dB) the output swing is 2 V p-p; -0.5 V on OFSx pre-biases it, and the ADC's 1 V VREF on VOCM centres it, so VOHx = 1.5 V and VOLx = 0.5 V at rest. VOLx drives the ADC's VIN+ and VOHx its VIN-, which inverts the negative pulse into the ADC's 0 V to 2 V range. VGAx still carries the negative pulse, 20 dB up.

parts.value: VGA output to other signal processing
other DAC outputs, to nine other AD8264s

notes: Channel x is drawn as channel 1 (IPP1, GNH1, OFS1, VGA1, VOL1, VOH1).
DAC outputs VOUT39, VOUT2, VOUT1 and VOUT0 feed the scale circuits of GNH1, GNH2, GNH3 and GNH4; the remaining outputs (VOUT4 onward) serve nine more AD8264s.
Each scale circuit draws 12.5 µA to 32.5 µA from its DAC output; about 250 nA flows in each GNHx pin.
VOUT = 2 × VREFIN × D / 2^N for the DAC.

Other gain control options: use the half of the DAC range from 0 V to 1.25 V with the Figure 112 divider (11 bits of gain resolution), or hold GNLO at another voltage between 625 mV and 1.2 V, such as 1 V, with the DAC running 0.375 V to 1.625 V.
U2 pins 1, 5 and 6 are NC.

circuits.title: AD8264-EVALZ evaluation board
circuits.description: The evaluation board: each input SMA (IN1 to IN4) is terminated in 49.9 Ω and reaches IPPx through a 0 Ω link. Each VGAx output reaches an SMA through 453 Ω, which protects the pin and can be shorted for more bandwidth. The differential outputs go through 0 Ω links to 2-pin headers at 0.1 in pitch for a low-capacitance differential probe. Preamp outputs are monitored in pairs through a selector switch and 453 Ω at OP1_2 and OP3_4. GNH1/GNH2 and GNH3/GNH4 are paired through 0 Ω links to test loops GN1_2 and GN34; VOCM and the paired OFSx pins each have a test loop and a 2-pin header whose jumper grounds them; GNLO has the header only. Each supply pin has a ferrite bead and 0.1 µF; each rail has 10 µF at its test loop.
notes: The board takes ±2.5 V to ±5 V from supplies able to deliver at least 400 mA: ground to a black test loop, positive to the red loop (+V), negative to the blue loop (-V).
It ships with jumpers on GN1_2, GN3_4, OFS_12, OFS_34, GNLO and VOCM; without them the offset and common-mode pins float high and the quiescent current rises sharply.
To drive an ADC, remove the offset jumpers and apply the offset at test loops OFS12 and OFS34; a buffered VOCM can go to the ADC reference.
Two parts carry the designator R17: the 49.9 Ω IN4 termination and the uninstalled part across GN3_4; the second is R17B.
Parts marked DNI are not installed.
Supply pins are named by number: 16 and 35 are VPOS, 17 and 34 are VNEG, 0, 12 and 39 are COMM.

operation.text: Each of the four identical channels runs a preamp with a fixed gain of 2 (6 dB), then a VGA made of a 0 dB to 24 dB attenuator ahead of a fixed 8× (18 dB) amplifier, then a single-ended-to-differential amplifier with a gain of 2 (6 dB). The gain from IPPx to VGAx spans 0 dB to 24 dB; to the differential output it spans 6 dB to 30 dB. Every stage is dc coupled, and the supplies run from ±2.5 V to ±5 V. The part is aimed at pulse processing such as PET imaging, and at any dc-coupled job needing variable gain.

The preamp is a current-feedback amplifier. IPPx is its high-impedance input; IPNx is normally left open. Its load is the pair of 100 Ω gain resistors inside plus the attenuator, about 113 Ω together. On ±5 V supplies it runs out of output current at 6 V p-p, so the input is limited to 3 V p-p there.

The VGA uses voltage feedback with analog gain control. Its small gain range keeps offset low and suits gain trimming. The preamp and VGA offsets are trimmed so the input-referred offset stays under 0.5 mV maximum across temperature. Keeping each stage's gain modest keeps the bandwidth high.

Gain is set by the differential voltage between each channel's GNHx and the GNLO pin shared by all four channels; GNLO must be biased and is normally grounded. The slope is 20 dB/V and the full range needs about ±0.65 V at GNHx relative to GNLO. With GNLO grounded GNHx may swing anywhere from VNEG to VPOS without gain foldover. GNLO's allowed range grows with supply: it must be at 0 V on ±2.5 V, may sit within ±1.2 V on ±3.3 V and within ±2.8 V on ±5 V. On 3.3 V, a quad single-supply DAC (such as the AD5314) can drive GNHx directly, with GNLO at half the DAC reference from a 2:1, 10 kΩ divider.

VGAx drives the noninverting input of the output amplifier, so the gain from IPPx is noninverting to VGAx and VOHx and inverting to VOLx. VOCM, common to the four amplifiers, sets the output common-mode voltage and must be driven: from an ADC's reference when feeding a dc-coupled ADC, or grounded when no level shift is needed. Each OFSx pin is the inverting input of its amplifier and sets a dc offset between the two outputs, which lets a unipolar pulse be mapped onto an ADC's full-scale range while staying dc coupled; ground OFSx when no offset is wanted, or use it as a separate input.

At maximum gain the preamp dominates: 2.3 nV/√Hz input-referred short-circuit noise counting every amplifier and gain resistor, or 2.1 nV/√Hz measured from VGAx, which leaves out the output amplifier. VGAx shows 34 nV/√Hz, doubled to 68 nV/√Hz by the output stage, which adds 26 nV/√Hz of its own for about 73 nV/√Hz differential. At minimum gain VGAx shows about 19 nV/√Hz and the differential output about 46 nV/√Hz. Input-referred noise rises as gain falls.

Input: 1.2 V p-p maximum on ±2.5 V, 2 V p-p on ±3.3 V to ±3.5 V, 3 V p-p on ±5 V (preamp drive limited). VGAx: 2.6 V p-p on ±2.5 V, 4 V p-p on ±3.3 V to ±3.5 V, 7.5 V p-p on ±5 V. The differential output, twice the VGA output, never limits first: 5.2 V p-p on ±2.5 V, 8 V p-p on ±3.3 V to ±3.5 V, 15 V p-p on ±5 V. Noise at the three points is 2.3 nV/√Hz at the input, 34 nV/√Hz at VGAx and 73 nV/√Hz at the differential output.

The part runs from ±2.5 V to ±5 V; on supplies above ±3.3 V the ambient is limited to -40 °C to +85 °C, otherwise -40 °C to +105 °C. Quiescent current is 79 mA typical on ±2.5 V, 85 mA on ±3.3 V and 99 mA on ±5 V (power 395 mW, 560 mW, 990 mW); the low-power figure is 140 mW per channel on ±3.3 V. VPOS pins 16 and 35 are tied inside, as are VNEG pins 17 and 34.

Safe dissipation is set by junction temperature. Near 150 °C, the glass transition of the plastic, the package's stress on the die changes; going past it even briefly can shift the amplifiers' parameters for good, and staying above 150 °C for long can cause loss of function.
The exposed pad (pin 0) is COMM and must be soldered to the ground plane for RF grounding and reliability; COMM also appears at pins 12 and 39.

Running from a bipolar supply lets the part amplify negative-going pulses, such as those a photodiode or photomultiplier makes by sinking current into a grounded load. Wideband video can also be processed without delay. With a multi-output DAC each of the four channels can calibrate actively or trim a gain.

To map a PMT's 0 V to -0.1 V pulse into a 0 V to 2 V ADC with 1 V common mode: set the gain to 20× (26 dB) for 2 V p-p, drive VOCM from the ADC's 1 V reference, and pre-bias OFSx at -0.5 V, giving VOHx = 1.5 V and VOLx = 0.5 V at rest. Connecting VOLx to the ADC's positive input and VOHx to its negative input inverts the pulse. A shared ADC reference should be buffered before it drives several AD8264s.

With a 0 V to 1.25 V DAC, bias GNLO at 625 mV (two 1 kΩ 1 % resistors from the 1.25 V reference) to reach the full 24 dB span. The roughly 1 µA from GNLO, or 2 µA for two parts on one divider, causes about 1 mV, 0.02 dB, of error, small beside the part's typical 0.2 dB gain error. With a 0 V to 2.5 V DAC: use half its range, or tie GNLO to ground and divide the DAC output down to -0.625 V to +0.625 V against -1.25 V, or hold GNLO at a voltage between 625 mV and 1.2 V (such as 1 V) and run the DAC from 0.375 V to 1.625 V. GNLO cannot simply be raised to 1.25 V because of its limited range.
